newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross gives WW2 archives to Jewish groups.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross gives WW2 archives to Jewish groups.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross has handed over microfilm of more than 40,000 pages of documents from its World War Two archives to the Jewish Holocaust Memorial in Washington, a spokesman said on Wednesday.

Kim Gordon-Bates said microchips of the same data -- 25,000 documents from ICRC archives -- would also be given to the Yad Vashem memorial in Jerusalem and the Jewish Contemporary Centre for Documentation in France.
He said the move had nothing to do with a Jewish dispute with the Swiss over the fate of bank accounts left ownerless by the Holocaust, the Nazi drive to eliminate the Jews.

The Swiss-run ICRC, which has been awarded the Nobel peace prize for its activities in defending war victims and political prisoners around the world, opened its archives from the wartime period to the public early last year.

The documents include data on the ICRC's contacts with Nazi officials to gain access to Jews in concentration camps and are just a tiny fraction of ICRC's archives on the World War Two, Gordon-Bates said.
